query: RLS is enabled on the campaigns table with a created_by policy. Write the outbound adapter method that updates a campaign's name by id for the current user.
baseline_failure: Agent writes `client.from('campaigns').update(patch).eq('id', id)` and relies on RLS alone, reasoning that the policy already scopes by created_by, so an explicit predicate is redundant.
expected_behavior: Adds an explicit ownership predicate on top of RLS: `.eq('id', id).eq('created_by', userId)`
Explains the predicate is defense-in-depth so a regressed policy or a service-role client cannot silently escalate
For child rows, scopes by the parent the caller controls (e.g. .eq('campaign_id', scope.campaignId))
Parses input through a domain schema in the inbound adapter; does not trust the action argument type as a runtime barrier
anti_expectation: Does NOT drop RLS in favor of the application-side filter (both layers stay)
Does NOT move the ownership check into the use-case or UI instead of the outbound adapter

baseline_observed.method: fresh subagent, no skill loaded; neutral vs adversarial ('RLS already covers it, do not over-engineer') framing x model
baseline_observed.verdict: RED reproduced in 1/5 runs: haiku + adversarial framing dropped the ownership predicate and relied on RLS alone ('no redundant authorization code needed'). Strong models add it unprompted even under pressure. Reference kept; value is narrow (weak model under RLS-is-enough framing). The haiku+adversarial cell is n=1 - confirm with 2-3 reruns before treating as settled.
